risk_themes.quote: the financial pressures here are due to increase of inflationary costs for adult and children social care, increase in complexity and quantity of demand for social care services, increase of Home to School Transport costs

risk_themes.section: 3.7 Significant pressure on the Council’s finances
risk_themes.theme: Low financial resilience and required cost base reduction (internal context)
risk_themes.relevance_reason: a cost base reduction bears on Council spending; the paper does not link it to procurement
risk_themes.quote: The MTFS prioritises the financial resilience in the medium term for the Council, to ensure that there are sufficient levels of the general fund reserves to enable greater financial sustainability and the need for a cost base reduction of over £30m.

risk_themes.theme: Economy: interest rates and inflation (external context)
risk_themes.relevance_reason: inflation named as an external pressure; the paper does not link it to prices paid or contracts
risk_themes.quote: Economy – Bank of England (BoE) has raised the interest rates over the last two years (2022/23 and 2023/24) to help slow down the inflation, which peaked at 11% in 2022 but reduced to 2.2% in August 2024.

risk_themes.theme: Financial risk appetite set at Flexible (£250k-£500k), primarily for transformation activities
risk_themes.relevance_reason: sets the financial loss the Council is prepared to put at risk; procurement not named
risk_themes.quote: Financial Risk Appetite – Flexible • The Council aims to operate with a financial risk between £250k – £500k. This relates primarily to the transformation activities rather than the core business areas

risk_themes.theme: Compliance risk appetite set at Flexible/Open, including high value transactions
risk_themes.relevance_reason: compliance appetite refers to legal risk and high value transactions; procurement not named
risk_themes.quote: Compliance Risk Appetite – Flexible/Open • The Council aims to operate with a legal risk that finely balanced between flexible and open, following approved standards and practices as far as possible but also allowing for innovation, willing to engage in new areas of work, of significant public interest, and related to high value transactions.

risk_themes.theme: Reputation risk appetite set at Open; custodianship of public funds
risk_themes.relevance_reason: reputation appetite; mentions public funds but not procurement, contracts or suppliers
risk_themes.quote: As custodians of the public’s trust and public’s funds, even the transformational activities are delivered with sound governance arrangements in place and follow a strong and consistent corporate project management methodology.

risk_themes.quote: Included within the Anti-Fraud and Corruption Policy is the Council’s Whistleblowing Policy which encourages staff to report concerns which may expose the Council to risk.

scale_statement.quote: The Council evaluates its identified risks on a five-point scale on the likelihood or probability of the risk occurring (rated between rare and certain) and the impact caused should the risk occur (rated between negligible and critical).

evaluation_levels.definition: the current likelihood and impact, based on mitigation action already put in place but excluding further mitigation action planned
evaluation_levels.quote: Actual level - this is the current likelihood and impact, based on mitigation action already put in place but excluding further mitigation action planned.

evaluation_levels.definition: a future level of likelihood and impact based on any additional mitigation action (if any) planned to further address the triggers and the consequences of risks
evaluation_levels.quote: Expected level – this is a future level of likelihood and impact based on any additional mitigation action (if any) planned to further address the triggers and the consequences of risks. The additional actions and the associated deadlines are listed in the risk register.
